payload.stem: How do relational database engines guarantee data integrity during Index Internals & Tuning under concurrent transactions?

options.text: Enforcing row-level locking or multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) snapshots
Flushing all tables to unencrypted text files
Executing all transactions in serial queue order globally

criteria.name: Concurrency Protocol
criteria.description: Correctly identifies MVCC or row locks.

model_answer: Option A is correct: relational engines use MVCC snapshots and selective row locks to provide ACID transaction guarantees.
explanation: MVCC allows readers to read consistent snapshots without blocking writers, while writers lock individual rows to prevent dirty writes.

payload.stem: Explain how deadlocks arise in database systems during Index Internals & Tuning and how applications should structure queries to avoid them.

criteria.name: Deadlock Cycle Theory
criteria.description: Identifies circular wait graphs between conflicting locks.

criteria.name: Deterministic Ordering
criteria.description: Recommends consistent global lock acquisition order.

model_answer: Deadlocks occur when two transactions each hold a lock the other requires, forming a circular wait graph. Applications prevent deadlocks by acquiring locks in consistent monotonic order (e.g. sorted by ID).
explanation: By enforcing a strict global ordering for multi-row operations, cyclic lock dependencies become impossible to form.
